subject: Clarify audit-log granularity & BYOK retention carveout
messages:
From: Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@stellamed.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: security@stellamed.com
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on audit log retention + BYOK handling

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo last week — StellaMed's security team had a few follow-ups for us to clarify before we proceed to a pilot. Two asks stood out:

1) Audit log retention granularity: we need to know whether Redwood can keep detailed request/response events for 90 days for a subset of traffic (pilot) while defaulting to 30 days for other traffic. Is per-customer retention windows configurable or do we only have global retention tiers?

2) BYOK / KMS carveouts: our legal team requires that audit records containing customer identifiers be excluded from any hosted key backup/escrow processes. Can Redwood support a carveout so audit logs referencing PII are retained only within our VPC/Dedicated environment and never copied to Redwood-managed backups?

Attached is a short list of questions from our security team (stella-security-questions.pdf). Can you loop in the right folks and let us know constraints and timelines?

Appreciate it —
Jorge
Jorge Ramos
Director, IT Security | StellaMed
jorge.ramos@stellamed.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.inference.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com
Cc: Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@stellamed.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on audit log retention + BYOK handling

Team — forwarding a quick security follow-up from StellaMed (attached). High level asks: 90-day retention for a pilot segment, and a BYOK carveout so audit events containing sensitive customer IDs never leave their Dedicated environment or are included in our managed backups.

Can each of you confirm:
- karthik: is there an existing exception path for "audit-only" exclusion from backup/escrow, or would this require a product change? Rough notes on technical feasibility would be great.
- tessa: operational impact for Dedicated vs Hosted (backup flows, escrow processes, retention config surface).
- marissa: commercial implications and timeline — do we have precedent for a pilot carveout and how that maps to pricing/SLA?

Goal: reply to Jorge with a short options list and proposed next steps by EOD tomorrow so they can decide whether to use Redwood Dedicated for the pilot.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>, tessa.morgan@redwood.inference.com, marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on audit log retention + BYOK handling

Irene / team — quick technical readout. Short answers first: feasible, but with caveats.

1) Retention by traffic segment: In Dedicated we already support customer-scoped retention knobs per deployment (config flags exposed via the private control plane). We can scope retention by route or by token prefix if the customer routes pilot traffic through a dedicated model route. For Hosted this is not currently exposed per-customer.

2) BYOK/backup carveout: Our current backup/escrow pipeline copies encrypted artifacts (including audit bundles) into Redwood-managed cold storage for 30/90/365-day retention policies. For Dedicated VPCs we can add a policy to mark audit bundles as "no-escrow" and keep them only on customer-managed storage endpoints, but this is not yet automated — it requires:
- a small infra change to add a "no-escrow" flag per audit bundle (backend + metadata)
- a one-time ops run to move existing pilot bundles to customer-supplied S3 (or enforce no-copy at generation time)

Risk/notes:
- Audit bundles often reference request metadata; to be airtight we recommend hashing or tokenizing customer identifiers prior to writing audit bundles if they must transit Redwood systems. If they must never transit, we should host audit logging ingestion entirely in-customer (VPC-only ingestion path).
- Timeline: product + infra change 6-8 weeks for automation (shorter if we do manual ops + gating for a single pilot: ~2 weeks).

I'm attaching a draft internal policy that outlines the exemption flow (kms-exemptions-policy-draft.docx). Happy to spin up a brief tech design meeting.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>, tessa.morgan@redwood.inference.com
Date: Tue, 16 Sep 2025 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on audit log retention + BYOK handling

Irene — from a commercial/CS perspective:
- We've done one pilot where we offered a 60-day pilot window for enhanced retention on Dedicated; that was priced as a small monthly uplift + one-time ops fee to handle migration of existing logs.
- If we take the manual ops route (2 weeks), recommend we charge a one-time $7.5k onboarding fee for the migration & to cover the engineering effort. If they want automation (6-8 weeks), we should treat that as a product roadmap item and discuss longer-term commercial terms.

Next step: I'll prepare a short options table (manual pilot vs automated product change) and a suggested SOW line item. Irene — if you can confirm the pilot start target, I can draft language for the quote.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@stellamed.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.inference.com
Date: Wed, 17 Sep 2025 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on audit log retention + BYOK handling

Jorge — thanks for the clear asks and the attached questions. Quick summary of options and recommended next steps: 

Option A — Short pilot (recommended, fastest):
- Run pilot in Redwood Dedicated with per-route retention set to 90 days for the pilot route; other traffic remains at our default 30 days.
- Carveout: we will mark pilot audit bundles with a manual "no-escrow" flag and move them to a customer-provided S3 bucket. This requires a short ops window (~2 weeks) and a one-time onboarding fee ($7.5k).

Option B — Product automation (longer-term):
- Implement automated "no-escrow" flags and per-customer retention config in the control plane. Estimated 6–8 weeks. This would remove the manual ops fee but needs product prioritization.

Technical notes (from our security lead):
- If StellaMed requires audit bundles with PII to never transit Redwood-managed storage, we can also enable VPC-only ingestion for the pilot so logs are written directly to your storage endpoint — will add complexity but is possible.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Confirm you want the short pilot and provide the S3 endpoint / IAM role for ingestion.
2) Marissa to send SOW line item for the one-time ops fee and pilot dates.
3) Karthik to schedule a 45-minute technical kickoff with your security engineer to confirm hashing/tokenization choices and ingestion path.

I've attached your original questions for reference and our internal policy draft. Let me know if you want me to schedule the kickoff (I can do Thurs or Fri this week).

Best —
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0183
